The independent development-only C# recipes in ../reference/list-interface.cs generate two corpora on Windows .NET Framework 4.0.30319.42000. Regenerate with Windows PowerShell and ../reference/generate-list-interface.ps1. No original Pascal compiler is invoked. Managed tools and sources are excluded from the native application package.

list-interface-reference.tsv contains 456 outcomes for arrays, List and a user-defined IList<int>. All thirteen inherited/own interface members are tested on empty/nonempty and null sources. CopyTo, indexed reads/writes, Insert, RemoveAt and compound indexed assignment vary negative, valid and past-end indices. The output records the complete custom Count/indexer/method/enumerator callback sequence. Compound assignment also traces receiver, index and right-hand-side evaluation. Framework's generic array IList indexer reports argument-range errors (E_RANGE), unlike direct native array indexing (E_BOUNDS). Fixed-size array Insert/RemoveAt report E_READONLY before checking the supplied index; assigning an existing item is allowed despite IsReadOnly being true.

school-ilist-reference.tsv contains 1152 outcomes. The recipe lowers the exact IList<string> ReplaceMany algorithm from bin/Lib/School.pas into StringBuilder calls: target.Count first, source.Count second, each once, then source[i] and target[i] in argument order. Nine source/target family combinations, four pattern arrays, four replacement arrays, null source/target and null initial text are covered. Custom traces distinguish source and target. Empty/nil patterns and nil replacements test both results and the point at which an error occurs. This proves the closed overload's selected behaviors; it does not expose StringBuilder as a completed native type.

Fields in each TSV are integer inputs for the corresponding independent native Pascal fixture, UTF-16 hex output (- means empty), and mapped native error code. ICollection errors map as in collection-interface-reference.md; generic array IList index errors map to E_RANGE. Each row starts from a fresh source and is executed by the separately compiled native fixture. Source/fixture/output hashes normalized to LF are in list-interface-reference.json.

Compound property assignment follows the local original compiler's TreeConverter/TreeConversion/SyntaxTreeVisitorNodes/Assign.cs:422–433 and 492–495, which embeds receiver/index expressions in both setter and getter calls. Case 13 explicitly lowers this into separate C# call arguments rather than using the different C# compound-assignment operator. Receiver/index callbacks therefore occur twice, including with array-backed IList. The longstanding scalar-property core expectation CCGRS is preserved.

Additional native checks exercise named/default multi-parameter properties on classes and inherited user interfaces, getter/setter type matching, write-only/readonly properties, properties returning arrays or indexed objects, repeated Pascal property operands in compound writes, type errors before output, interface casts, List version invalidation, work limits and malformed metadata. General generic source classes/routines, record interface boxing, complete object/exception support, readonly collection interfaces and every imported API remain open. PABCSystem, Collections and School remain partial modules.
